short: Large-deformation plasticity and fracture behavior of pure l
title: Large-deformation plasticity and fracture behavior of pure lithium under various stress states

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Lithium-metal cells need a quantitative large-deformation and fracture description of pure Li. Li's plasticity and fracture over stress states from simple shear to triaxial tension are unmeasured at the meso-scale.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/gap), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/method), n5 (DES/variable_sweep), n6 (PRC/forming), n7 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Deformation runs by slip: straight traces of two active slip systems inside single grains, stopping at the boundaries. Grains thin continuously until the local thickness reaches zero and the fracture surface collapses to a line

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Wavy slip lines identify cross-slip as active already at room temperature, as expected for Li's low melting point. Pure Li fails by perfectly ductile fracture: separation by sliding, no dimples, no crack initiation in shear.
states.detail: Absorbed: n11 (MEC/identification), n13 (PRP/behavior_class), n14 (PRP/value), n15 (PRP/value), n16 (PRP/value), n17 (MEC/tradeoff), n18 (PRP/value), n19 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Wavy slip lines are the signature of cross-slip, seen in other metals at high homologous temperature; LePage et al.: Li foil is transversely isotropic with a [100] normal-direction texture, peak stress ~0.8 MPa and n = 6.55; Hill48 anisotropic yield function with Voce hardening and a power-law rate term; ten parameters, four fitted; A previously developed specimen set (refs 46,47): notch radii and a central hole impose defined triaxial stress states

states.title: Performance state
states.head: A transverse-isotropic Hill48 model with Voce hardening and rate dependence, calibrated on four tests, reproduces all five force-displacement curves
states.detail: Absorbed: n20 (PRF/service_capability). Premises: Hill48 anisotropic yield function with Voce hardening and a power-law rate term; ten parameters, four fitted

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Pure Li is perfectly ductile from shear to triaxial tension; small hardening, strong rate strengthening and through-thickness anisotropy set its large-deformation response

nodes.title: MICRO, F4
nodes.head: After seconds of air only a few bright particles sit on otherwise bare grains; after 5 min bright product covers the field in extended chains
nodes.note: in the 5 min panel the chains are marked by four dashed overlays; whether they are truly connected is not resolvable at 10 um scale
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and n14 keeps shown support from o2, o3, o5.

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: The 0, 1 and 10 min curves superpose with a 1.2 MPa peak; the 60 min curve peaks at 1.41 MPa and lies above them to 0.55 strain
nodes.solves: Engineering stress peaks near 1.2 MPa at about 0.05 nominal strain and then falls monotonically: strain hardening is small
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: fracture strain is not monotone in exposure time: 0 min ends at ~0.72, 10 min ~0.75, but 1 min ~0.95 and 60 min ~0.95; all curves fall smoothly to zero with no sharp drop
nodes.detail: o3: The 0, 1 and 10 min curves superpose with a 1.2 MPa peak; the 60 min curve peaks at 1.41 MPa and lies above them to 0.55 strain

nodes.title: MICRO, F6
nodes.head: Inside one deformed grain two sets of straight parallel line traces cross at a shallow angle. The side profile tapers to a knife edge, the fracture line running at mid-thickness from one edge to the other
nodes.solves: Deformation runs by slip: straight traces of two active slip systems inside single grains, stopping at the boundaries
nodes.note: the two sets are marked by dashed and dotted yellow overlays; the cracked surface layer follows the steps dashed overlay marks the fracture line at mid-thickness of the 500 um overview; the two halves meet in a point

nodes.solves: Grains thin continuously until the local thickness reaches zero and the fracture surface collapses to a line
nodes.note: side view at 1 mm scale; the lower surface is heavily wrinkled, consistent with the reaction products the text reports from the transfer

nodes.title: MICRO, F1

nodes.title: MICRO, F6
nodes.head: Elsewhere the slip traces are not straight but wavy, curving within the grain. In the magnified area the fracture surface is smooth sliding relief with no dimples
nodes.solves: Wavy slip lines identify cross-slip as active already at room temperature, as expected for Li's low melting point
nodes.note: a band of short dashed overlays marks the wavy traces beside a long raised ridge crossing the field the 100 um inset of the same panel; the surface is featureless apart from sliding relief, with no voids or dimples

nodes.title: evidence, F5
nodes.head: Fracture displacement falls across the notched series: about 3.4 mm at R10, 2.4 mm at R5 and 2.0 mm for the central hole
nodes.solves: Fracture displacement falls as the stress state becomes more triaxial: about 3.4 mm (R10), 2.4 mm (R5), 2.0 mm (central hole)
nodes.note: the central-hole force is highest (peak ~8 N) because its gauge is 8 mm wide against 5 mm; whole figure read, F5 offers no panels
nodes.detail: o6: Fracture displacement falls across the notched series: about 3.4 mm at R10, 2.4 mm at R5 and 2.0 mm for the central hole
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n18 (o6).

nodes.title: evidence, F10, F5
nodes.head: At 0.7 nominal strain the plastic strain in thickness has reached about 0.48 while the width strain is only about 0.12. For notched R10 the rate-dependent isotropic simulation runs about 0.3-0.4 N above the data from 0.6 mm onward.
nodes.solves: Through-thickness plastic strain grows about four times faster than width strain: strong through-thickness anisotropy
nodes.op: compare across conditions, compare coplotted quantities, overlay model on data
nodes.note: per the caption the width strain is measured by DIC and the thickness strain calculated; both are plotted on the same right-hand axis against the blue stress curve at 2.0 mm the isotropic dashed curve reads ~4.9 N against ~4.6 N measured; the rate-dependent anisotropic curve sits on the data over the whole range both loci pass through (+/-1, 0) and (0, +/-1); the difference is largest along sigma_1 = sigma_2 and sigma_1 = -sigma_2
nodes.detail: o7: At 0.7 nominal strain the plastic strain in thickness has reached about 0.48 while the width strain is only about 0.12; o13: For notched R10 the rate-dependent isotropic simulation runs about 0.3-0.4 N above the data from 0.6 mm onward; o15: The calibrated Hill48 yield locus is pulled in near equibiaxial tension (1.0 vs 1.15) and pushed out in the shear quadrant, meeting von Mises at the uniaxial points
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n15 (o7, o13, o15).

nodes.title: MECH:tensile, F5
nodes.head: In simple shear the force rises monotonically to about 1.75 N at 2.5-2.8 mm with no drop, then falls only at separation near 3.4-4.7 mm
nodes.solves: Pure Li fails by perfectly ductile fracture: separation by sliding, no dimples, no crack initiation in shear
nodes.note: the three shear repeats scatter far more than the tensile-type tests, separating between 3.4 and 4.7 mm; whole figure read, F5 offers no panels
nodes.detail: o8: In simple shear the force rises monotonically to about 1.75 N at 2.5-2.8 mm with no drop, then falls only at separation near 3.4-4.7 mm
nodes.necessity_reason: n13 keeps shown support from o17 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F10
nodes.head: The rate-independent anisotropic simulation peaks at 0.3 mm and then collapses to about 0.3 N by 3 mm, where the test still carries 3.5 N
nodes.solves: Rate strengthening is significant: without it the material loses the load-carrying capacity the test retains after necking
nodes.note: the collapse is already complete by ~1.5 mm; the green inset shapes show the corresponding thickness reduction
nodes.detail: o14: The rate-independent anisotropic simulation peaks at 0.3 mm and then collapses to about 0.3 N by 3 mm, where the test still carries 3.5 N
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n16 (o14).

nodes.title: MECH:tensile, F9
nodes.head: Simulated curves track the measured points of all five tests, including the uniaxial tension test held back for validation
nodes.solves: A transverse-isotropic Hill48 model with Voce hardening and rate dependence, calibrated on four tests, reproduces all five force-displacement curves
nodes.note: agreement is closest for notched R10 and uniaxial tension; the central-hole simulation runs ~0.5 N high past 1.2 mm, and every simulated curve stops short of the measured end point
nodes.detail: o12: Simulated curves track the measured points of all five tests, including the uniaxial tension test held back for validation
